title: The WordPress provision reads plugin answers from a file: a 1.5 MB inspect answer confirms the binding, and a check that dies silently still says why
steps: S1: From the checkout run: node --test --test-concurrency=1 packages/fleet/tracy-fleet-operation/test/wordpress-quickstart.test.mjs
S2: Read the exit code and the fail count.
expect: The test 'a bind or inspect answer that is not JSON says what curl saw, and never the token' passes, including its 1.5 MB inspect answer that must print 'inspect: bound, 60 entities'.
The test 'an inspect check that dies without a word still says why it failed' passes: the reason reads 'the inspect answer could not be read (python3 exit 126)', never empty.
evidence: 09/11/2026: the JA Diner wp7 demo, updated to 1.0.3, ended 'Failed at provision' with 'inspect after bind:' and no reason. Its inspect answer was 143,759 bytes; python3 was handed it as one argument and Linux refused to start it (Argument list too long, exit 126).
fence: The real wordpress.sh against a local HTTP double of the plugin door. Not exercised: a real WordPress site or a full provision run.
